title: partialPrefetching
description: Configure the default link prefetch behavior to fetch only the static parts of each route.
url: "https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching"
docs_index: /docs/llms.txt
lastUpdated: 2026-10-02
prerequisites:
  - "Configuration: /docs/app/api-reference/config"
  - "next.config.js: /docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js"
related:
  - /docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents
  - /docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/prefetch
  - /docs/app/api-reference/components/link
  - /docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching
---

> For an index of all documentation, see [/docs/llms.txt](/docs/llms.txt).

`partialPrefetching` enables Partial Prefetching at the app level. The framework prefetches the static parts of each route by default; set `prefetch={true}` on individual links to use [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) and fetch more.

## Usage

**TypeScript**

```ts highlight={5} title="next.config.ts" 
import type { NextConfig } from 'next'

const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
  cacheComponents: true,
  partialPrefetching: true,
}

export default nextConfig
```

**JavaScript**

```js highlight={3} title="next.config.js" 
module.exports = {
  cacheComponents: true,
  partialPrefetching: true,
}
```

`partialPrefetching` requires [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents). Without it, `next dev` and `next build` throw at config validation.

## Reference

| Value   | Description                                                                                                            |
| ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `true`  | Enables Partial Prefetching across the app.                                                                            |
| `false` | Keeps the previous prefetch behavior, for apps that adopted Cache Components before Partial Prefetching was available. |

Leaving the option unset behaves like `false` and logs a warning when `cacheComponents` is enabled. Both features will be enabled everywhere in the next major release, and the options will be removed.

## How prefetches resolve

Before Partial Prefetching, Next.js prefetched per visible link: a page with N links to N routes produced \~N route prefetches as those links entered the viewport.

With `partialPrefetching: true`, Next.js prefetches one reusable [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell) per route instead. The App Shell contains rendered output that does not depend on a link's URL. URL-specific content, including content that depends on `params` or `searchParams`, resolves after navigation by default. App Shells are cached on the client, so links to the same route reuse one prefetch.

The pattern is similar to per-route code splitting in single-page apps: one artifact per route, shared by every link that points to it.

> **Good to know:**
>
> Routes that read `cookies()` or `headers()` produce an App Shell that includes session data. The framework auto-detects this and caches the shell per session on the client.

A link can ask for more than the App Shell with [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link#prefetch). The prefetch also resolves URL data like `params`, `searchParams`, and the full URL, and the cached content behind it. See [Optimizing prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching).

> **Good to know:**
>
> If you use `<Link prefetch={true}>` to a route that hasn't opted into Partial Prefetching, a dev console error suggests enabling `partialPrefetching` app-wide or `prefetch = 'partial'` on the segment. The [dev warning Insight](/docs/messages/instant-link-prefetch-partial) covers each fix in detail.

## Per-segment overrides

A segment that exports an explicit [`prefetch`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/prefetch) value overrides the app-level default for that route.

## Version History

| Version | Change                                                                     |
| ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 16.3.0  | `partialPrefetching` introduced. Requires `cacheComponents` to be enabled. |

- [prefetch config](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/prefetch): Configure how a route segment is prefetched during client navigation.
- [Link Component](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link): Enable fast client-side navigation with the built-in \`next/link\` component.
- [Optimizing prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching): Resolve per-link URL data, include session data in the App Shell, or defer expensive work to a later navigation stage.

) } async function getTopics(team: string | undefined) { 'use cache' return db.topics.forTeam(team) } ``` On a direct visit, `` shows its fallback until the lookup resolves. On navigation, the App Shell has already resolved it, because the team cookie is session data the shell can read. Because sessions on the same team share the cache entry, traffic to the underlying data scales with team count, not session count. Anything without a caching directive still streams in after navigation. A shell holds only what can be prepared ahead of the navigation, not the whole page. It advances only as far as the caching structure allows. ### `"use cache: private"` When the lookup is tied to a single session, use [`"use cache: private"`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-private). It assigns a cache lifetime to a function that reads cookies, headers, or other runtime data directly. Results are cached in the browser only, scoped to that session. ```tsx title="app/dashboard/user-nav.tsx" import { cookies } from 'next/headers' async function UserNav() { const user = await getUser() return
{user.name}
} async function getUser() { 'use cache: private' const session = (await cookies()).get('session')?.value return db.users.findBySession(session) } ``` Here `cookies()` lives inside the cached function, which only works under `"use cache: private"`. Use the same pattern when runtime data cannot be extracted at the call site. For example, an authentication helper may compare `Date.now()` with a token's expiration, or a session helper may read cookies within its own code. Everything inside the scope shares the same lifetime. Colocate `"use cache: private"` as close to the runtime data access as possible. ## Defer work to a later stage The App Shell is shared by the links into a route. A per-link prefetch runs for a visible ``, and the navigation runs when the user clicks. Expensive work may not be worth generating for links the user never follows. Uncached work is already left out of prefetches. For cacheable work, `next/cache` exports functions that defer the code below each call: - [`prefetch()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/prefetch) defers the code until a per-link prefetch or navigation. - [`navigation()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/navigation) defers the code until navigation. In the following diagram, a gray dashed outline marks the Suspense fallback, while blue marks the deferred work once it renders: ![The Shell, Prefetch, and Navigation stages, with bars showing that work below prefetch() renders from the per-link prefetch onward and work below navigation() renders only during navigation, while earlier stages show the Suspense fallback](/docs/light/navigation-stage-visual.png) Both functions apply only during runtime rendering, so they do not change a fully static route. Each call defers the component that awaits it and that component's descendants. Earlier stages render the nearest [``](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense) fallback, which the deferred subtree replaces when its stage runs. Unlike [`connection()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/connection), neither function makes the subtree request-dependent, so functions within it can still use `use cache`. See [How `navigation()` differs from `connection()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/navigation#how-navigation-differs-from-connection). ### Keep expensive session data out of the App Shell Take the dashboard again. A ranking keyed on the session is expensive, and every default `` into the dashboard would generate it for the shell. Await `prefetch()` above the ranking so that only a `` resolves it before the click: ```tsx highlight={6} title="app/dashboard/recommendations.tsx"

--- title: navigation description: Defer runtime work until the user navigates with the navigation function. url: "https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/functions/navigation" docs_index: /docs/llms.txt lastUpdated: 2026-10-15 navTitle: "navigation" prerequisites: - "API Reference: /docs/app/api-reference" - "Functions: /docs/app/api-reference/functions" related: - /docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching - /docs/app/guides/keeping-pages-static - /docs/app/api-reference/functions/prefetch - /docs/app/api-reference/functions/connection - /docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching --- > For an index of all documentation, see [/docs/llms.txt](/docs/llms.txt). Calling `await navigation()` keeps runtime work below it out of the [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell) and per-link prefetches. The work runs when the user navigates, while the fallback of the nearest [``](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense) boundary renders in the prefetched output. Use `navigation()` for reusable content that is expensive to generate and should wait until navigation. Static prerenders still include the content in their output, so it can appear in a static prefetch. ## Usage The function requires [Cache Components](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents), and throws without it. It is meant for routes using [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching), which you can enable globally or one route at a time by [adopting Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching). ```ts highlight={4,5} title="next.config.ts" import type { NextConfig } from 'next' const nextConfig: NextConfig = { cacheComponents: true, partialPrefetching: true, } export default nextConfig ``` With Partial Prefetching enabled, Next.js loads server-rendered output in stages, before and during a client navigation. These are the route's [navigation stages](/docs/app/glossary#navigation-stages): 1. A default `` loads the [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell), which holds the part of the route that does not depend on the URL. 2. An optional [``](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link#prefetch) can also load content that depends on the link's URL. 3. When the user follows the link, the navigation renders the rest of the route. During runtime rendering, awaiting `navigation()` keeps content out of the App Shell and per-link prefetches, so it renders during navigation. Static prerenders can still include the content. Without Partial Prefetching, `navigation()` still defers the content for a default ``, but [``](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link#prefetch) fetches the whole route, deferred content included, the same as a navigation. To keep content out of the App Shell while still including it in a per-link prefetch, use [`prefetch()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/prefetch). > **Good to know:** > > `navigation()` defers one subtree. To require a static App Shell and static per-link prefetches across the route, use [`ensureStatic = 'prefetch'`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/ensureStatic#prefetch). See [Keeping pages static](/docs/app/guides/keeping-pages-static) for a worked example. Everything above `navigation()` can render in the App Shell or a per-link prefetch, while everything below waits for navigation. Deferral is scoped to the component that awaits it and the tree below: sibling branches keep their existing behavior. Place it above the code to defer, and wrap the component in [``](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense): **TypeScript** ```tsx highlight={20} title="app/post/[slug]/page.tsx" import { Suspense } from 'react' import { cookies } from 'next/headers' import { cacheLife, navigation } from 'next/cache' export default function Page({ params }: PageProps<'/post/[slug]'>) { return ( <> Loading post...

}> {/* in a per-link prefetch */} Loading comments...

}> {/* the fallback is in the prefetch, the comments are not */} ) } async function Comments({ params }: { params: Promise<{ slug: string }> }) { await navigation() // runtime work below renders on navigation const { slug } = await params const sort = (await cookies()).get('comment-sort')?.value ?? 'newest' const items = await getComments(slug, sort) return } async function getComments(slug: string, sort: string) { 'use cache' cacheLife('hours') return db.comments.list({ slug, sort }) } ``` **JavaScript** ```jsx highlight={20} title="app/post/[slug]/page.js" import { Suspense } from 'react' import { cookies } from 'next/headers' import { cacheLife, navigation } from 'next/cache' export default function Page({ params }) { return ( <> Loading post...

}> {/* in a per-link prefetch */} Loading comments...

}> {/* the fallback is in the prefetch, the comments are not */} ) } async function Comments({ params }) { await navigation() // runtime work below renders on navigation const { slug } = await params const sort = (await cookies()).get('comment-sort')?.value ?? 'newest' const items = await getComments(slug, sort) return } async function getComments(slug, sort) { 'use cache' cacheLife('hours') return db.comments.list({ slug, sort }) } ``` Comments are fetched by slug, so prefetching them would take a per-link prefetch. Awaiting `navigation()` before that data access keeps them out of the prefetch, so they render when the user navigates. The slug and the cookie are both read below `navigation()` and passed as arguments, so `getComments` caches per post and sort order rather than per visitor. The URL is resolved by the time the deferred content renders, so `params` is available below `navigation()`. Put the directive on a function called below it, as `getComments` does here. Awaiting `navigation()` inside a cached scope, such as [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) or [`use cache: private`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-private), is not allowed. ## How `navigation()` differs from `connection()` The [`connection()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/connection) function waits for a real request. It excludes the code that follows from prerendering and prefetching, making that work request-dependent. Awaiting `navigation()` excludes the code that follows from route prefetches. It resolves when the user navigates without making that work request-dependent. A function called after `await navigation()` can therefore use [`"use cache"`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) and keep its cache lifetime without generating its result during prefetching. Use `connection()` when the work must run for a real request. Use `navigation()` when the work is reusable but should wait until the user navigates. ## When to use it Use `navigation()` when the content below it is expensive to produce and no prefetch should generate it. Neither the runtime App Shell nor a runtime per-link prefetch runs that code, so its upstream requests are not issued until the user navigates. Leaving content uncached also keeps it out of prefetches, but gives up its cache lifetime. With `navigation()` the content can be cached with [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache), given a lifetime, and deferred to the navigation. Give it a [`stale`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife#stale) time of five minutes or more and the client-side router reuses it after the first time a user navigates into the route. Below that, a [short lifetime keeps it out of the App Shell](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife#prerendering-behavior), so each navigation fetches it again. ### Keeping a route's prefetch static When every read of [`cookies()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cookies), [`headers()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/headers), `params`, and `searchParams` sits below `navigation()`, the prerender a prefetch would trigger cannot produce more than the static output the build already generated, so the prefetch is served from that output instead. Shaping a route this way is an optional optimization: a static response can be cached in a CDN, so a link into the route costs no server CPU at all. ```tsx highlight={17} title="app/feed/page.tsx" import { Suspense } from 'react' import { cookies } from 'next/headers' import { navigation } from 'next/cache' export default function Page() { return ( <> {/* static, and so is the whole prefetch */} Loading stories...

}> ) } async function Stories() { await navigation() const topic = (await cookies()).get('topic')?.value ?? 'all' return } ``` ## Good to know - The function has no effect on the initial load of a page. - Reading `cookies()` or `headers()` below `navigation()` does not make the route's prefetches render per request, so they can still be served from static output. Those accesses are ignored, because they would not have resolved in a prefetch either. - A call outside a `` boundary surfaces an [Instant Insight](/docs/messages/instant-navigation-stage) in development. A fully prerendered route is unaffected, but the insight identifies that the call would defer content without a fallback if the route later requires runtime rendering. - Calling it inside `use cache`, `use cache: private`, [`unstable_cache()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/unstable_cache), [`after()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/after), [`generateStaticParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-static-params), or a Client Component throws. ## Reference ### Type ```ts function navigation(): Promise ``` ### Parameters - The function does not accept any parameters. ### Returns A `Promise`. It is not meant to be consumed. ## Version History | Version | Changes | | --------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `v16.4.0` | `navigation` introduced, replacing the `unstable_navigation` name used in earlier canary releases. | - [Optimizing prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching): Resolve per-link URL data, include session data in the App Shell, or defer expensive work to a later navigation stage. - [Keeping pages static](/docs/app/guides/keeping-pages-static): Keep selected route output static as your app changes. - [prefetch](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/prefetch): Defer runtime work until a per-link prefetch or navigation with the prefetch function. - [connection](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/connection): API Reference for the connection function. - [partialPrefetching](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching): Configure the default link prefetch behavior to fetch only the static parts of each route.

item.text:
The dashboard now prefetches each project’s cached title, so it can appear as soon as navigation starts. The description and activity stay behind a separate loading boundary and are requested when the user opens the project.

I enabled partial prefetching in [next.config.ts](/workspace/next.config.ts:3), opted the dashboard links into per-project prefetching in [app/page.tsx](/workspace/app/page.tsx:15), and split the title from the deferred details in [app/projects/[slug]/page.tsx](/workspace/app/projects/[slug]/page.tsx:5).

The production build passes. I also checked the responses: the prefetch contains “Acme Storefront” but no description or activity; the navigation response contains the details.
